answer.worked:
At $x=1$, $y=-3\times1=-3$. At $x=2$, $y=-3\times2=-6$. Hence
$$\begin{aligned}\text{gradient}&=\frac{-6-(-3)}{2-1}\\&=-3\end{aligned}$$

At $x=1$, $y=-4\times1+2=-2$. At $x=2$, $y=-4\times2+2=-6$. Hence
$$\begin{aligned}\text{gradient}&=\frac{-6-(-2)}{2-1}\\&=-4\end{aligned}$$

At $x=1$, $y=-2\times1+5=3$. At $x=2$, $y=-2\times2+5=1$. Hence
$$\begin{aligned}\text{gradient}&=\frac{1-(3)}{2-1}\\&=-2\end{aligned}$$

At $x=1$, $y=-1\times1+2=1$. At $x=2$, $y=-1\times2+2=0$. Hence
$$\begin{aligned}\text{gradient}&=\frac{0-(1)}{2-1}\\&=-1\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: Describe a translation that moves the graph of $y=3x$ to the graph of $y=3x+3$.

answer.worked: Adding 3 to every y-value moves the graph vertically 3 units upwards.

children.prompt: Find a second translation that does this.

children.prompt: How many such translations are there?

entries.description:
Straight-line graphs that pass through the origin

We have seen that when we determine a table of values from a rule such as y = 2x (or y = 3x or y = −x), the points lie on a line. That is, we can draw a line through the points. The line is said to be the graph of y = 2x (or y = 3x or y = −x).

Since two points determine a line uniquely, we require two coordinate pairs that satisfy the equation. For y = 2x, the values x = 0 and x = 1 are suitable.

entries.description:
In summary, to find the gradient of a line we follow these steps.
• Find a point on the line.
• Move along the line by moving 1 unit to the right in the horizontal direction.
• Find the change in the y-coordinate that has occurred. This gives the gradient of the line.

entries.description:
Substitute an x value to find one point on the line.
If we put x = 1, this gives y = −2. So (1, 2) is a point on the line.
Substitute another x value to find a second point on the line.
If we put x = 2, this gives y = 5. So (2, 5) is another point on the line.
The change in the y-coordinates is 5 − 2 = 3 when we move 1 unit in the positive x-direction.
Hence, the gradient of the line is 3.

entries.description:
First, put x = 0. This gives y = 5, so (0, 5) is a point on the line.
Now move 1 unit to the right in the horizontal direction.
We get x = 1 and y = −3 × 1 + 5 = 2. So (1, 2) is another point on the line.
The change in y is 2 − 5 = −3, so the gradient is −3.
